name: Fitness Professional and Exercise Physiologist
description: ⚠⚠⚠ The entry-level education for this occupation is a HIGH SCHOOL DIPLOMA, and it has about 68,000 openings a year — one of the largest figures on this site. What the job requires is a CERTIFICATION, not a degree. ⚠⚠ So a Florida student in a kinesiology degree needs an answer to a direct question: what is the degree for? There are three good ones — clinical exercise physiology ($59,460, +13%), graduate school in a health profession, or management — and this page is organised around them.
credentialNote: ⚠⚠⚠ NO FLORIDA LICENCE FOR PERSONAL TRAINING AND NO PROGRAMMATIC ACCREDITOR FOR THE DEGREE. What employers and insurers check is a CERTIFICATION, and the recognised mark is that the certifying body itself is NCCA-accredited — ACSM, NASM, ACE and NSCA among them. BLS: "personal trainers usually must be certified before they begin working with clients." ⚠⚠ So a four-year graduate and a certified trainer with no degree compete for the same floor job, and the certification is the part that is checked. ⚠ THE DEGREE PAYS OFF ONE LEVEL UP — clinical exercise physiology, cardiac rehabilitation, collegiate strength and conditioning, corporate wellness design, and graduate school. Those roles do read the transcript. ⚠⚠ Exercise physiology is licensed in only one state (Louisiana), so in Florida the clinical gate is the employer's requirement; ask which certification they want BEFORE choosing an exam. ⚠⚠⚠ AND KNOW THE LEGAL EDGE OF THE JOB: dietetics is LICENSED in Florida, so nutrition advice beyond general guidance is regulated, whatever your certification says.

cipCodes.note: ⚠⚠ Allied Health Diagnostic and Treatment Professions — named because athletic training lives here and is the credentialled neighbour: master's-level entry, programmatically accredited and LICENSED in Florida. ⚠ An undergraduate PET or APK course does not accumulate toward it, so work backwards from a target programme's prerequisite list.

⚠⚠⚠ Rehabilitation and Therapeutic Professions — where a large share of exercise science students are actually heading. ⚠ The decisive prerequisite is anatomy BY NUMBER: DPT programmes name BSC2085C/BSC2086C, and the APK version taught in kinesiology departments is not reliably accepted in its place.

⚠ Dietetics and Clinical Nutrition — named for a legal reason rather than a thematic one. Nutrition is the first thing a client asks about and dietetics is licensed in Florida, so a trainer has a statutory limit on the advice they may give.

programs.note: The programme — and the note there is the one to read first, because the LARGER of the two degrees sharing this classification is sport MANAGEMENT, a business degree, and UF and Florida State award only that one.

⚠⚠ The credentialled version of the sideline role: master's entry, accredited, and licensed in Florida. A genuine destination for kinesiology graduates and one that must be planned for from the first year.
⚠⚠⚠ The commonest graduate destination out of exercise science. ⚠ Take the BSC anatomy sequence, not the APK one, or the application may fail on a prerequisite technicality.

⚠ Named because it is licensed in Florida and therefore marks the legal boundary of what a fitness professional may advise — and because the two credentials together are a much stronger practice than either alone.
⚠ A salaried route out that uses the training: worksite wellness, chronic-disease prevention and community physical activity, funded institutionally rather than client by client.
⚠ Named because the top of this occupation's wage table is management and self-employment, and because the larger degree in this family is already a business degree.

courses.reason: Anatomy and Physiology I — twenty carriers. ⚠⚠⚠ TAKE THIS NUMBER, not the kinesiology-department alternative. Nearly every Florida health-professions programme names the BSC sequence in its prerequisites, and a large share of exercise science students end up applying to one.
courses.variantNote: ⚠⚠⚠ The same subject is taught as APK2100C/APK2105C in kinesiology departments, and this site has recorded that divergence as the most damaging in Florida: the APK version is NOT reliably accepted where BSC is named. ⚠ BSC2085C is the equivalent integrated four-credit packaging at seven institutions.

courses.reason: Anatomy and Physiology II — the second half, and the one covering cardiovascular, respiratory and renal systems. ⚠ That is the physiology exercise science is actually built on, and the half a student who stops after the first course is missing.

Exercise Physiology I — FIU, USF and UWF. ⚠⚠ The core science of the degree: how the body responds to and adapts to exercise, energy systems, cardiovascular and respiratory response, training adaptation. ⚠ It is what separates an exercise science graduate from a certified trainer, and it is what the clinical roles read.

Exercise Physiology II — FGCU, FIU, UCF and UF. The advanced treatment: environmental physiology, ergogenic aids, special populations, chronic disease. ⚠⚠ This is the course that points at the EXERCISE PHYSIOLOGIST role — $59,460 median, +13% growth, the fastest in this family.

Exercise Prescription — FIU, UNF and UWF. Designing programmes for real people with real limitations, against published guidelines. ⚠ It is the single most directly employable course in the APK prefix, and the one a cardiac rehabilitation or corporate wellness employer will ask about.
Exercise Testing — FAU, UNF and USF. Graded exercise testing, VO2 assessment, body composition, interpretation. ⚠⚠ The hands-on assessment course, and the skill that justifies a clinical wage.
courses.variantNote: ⚠⚠⚠ NOT AUTOMATICALLY TRANSFERABLE — one of 13 PET numbers out of 122 that carry that statewide classification, against roughly 2% in a typical prefix. A receiving programme must attest to your competence itself. ⚠ Take it at the institution you will graduate from.

courses.reason: Physical Fitness Assessment and Exercise Prescription — the assessment-plus-prescription pairing under the PET prefix. ⚠ Where APK4125 is the science of prescription, this is the applied protocol version, and it is the closer match to what a fitness facility actually does.
courses.variantNote: ⚠⚠ Also NOT AUTOMATICALLY TRANSFERABLE, and PET3551 is a 3000-level twin of the same subject. Check which your programme names and take it late rather than early.

courses.reason: Nutrition for Sport and Exercise Science — FIU, UCF and UWF. ⚠⚠⚠ Nutrition is the first question every client asks and the one a trainer is most likely to answer unlawfully. Dietetics is LICENSED in Florida, so there is a legal limit on advice beyond general guidance. ⚠ Take this course to learn where the limit is as much as to learn the content.

Fundamentals of Human Nutrition — the lower-division nutrition course, widely carried and usually transferable. ⚠ Named as the accessible alternative where APK4163 is not offered, and because it is a prerequisite for several dietetics and health-professions routes.

Care and Prevention of Athletic Injuries — NINE public carriers, the widest course in this family. Recognition, first response, taping, return-to-activity judgement. ⚠ Practical, immediately useful, and the course that makes you employable in a school, club or team setting while still a student.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ PET2622C is the integrated form at Central Florida, Florida State, Tallahassee and Valencia — equivalent packaging, and no institution carries both.

courses.reason: Sport Psychology — FIU, Florida State and USF. Motivation, adherence, goal setting and behaviour change. ⚠⚠ Adherence is the actual problem in this profession: the technical programme is rarely what fails, and the clients who stay are what a self-employed trainer's income is made of.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ PET2210 Sport Psychology is a lower-division treatment at FSCJ, Lake-Sumter and Tallahassee.

courses.reason: Research and Evaluation in Kinesiology — FGCU, FIU and UF. Reading the literature, evaluating a claim, designing an assessment. ⚠⚠ The fitness industry runs on unevidenced claims, and the ability to tell a real study from a marketing one is a genuine professional differentiator — and the course a graduate programme looks for.

Statistical Methods I — thirty-nine carriers and (GE CORE). ⚠ Assessment is measurement: body composition, VO2, strength testing and progress tracking are all statistics, and so is every claim made about a training programme. ⚠⚠ It is a general-education requirement anyway, so it costs nothing to take it seriously.

General Psychology — widely carried and (GE CORE) at most institutions. ⚠ Named because behaviour change is the job, and because it is a prerequisite for the sport psychology and health behaviour courses as well as for most health-professions graduate programmes.

Organization and Administration of Physical Education and Sport — FAMU, FIU, UCF and USF. Budgets, staffing, risk management, facility operations. ⚠⚠ The people earning the 75th and 90th percentile wages in this occupation are mostly managing or self-employed, and this is the only course on the list that addresses that directly.

Sports and Fitness Internship — FAU, FIU and USF. ⚠⚠ In a field where the entry-level job needs no degree, demonstrated experience is what a degree-holder has to bring. ⚠ Choose the placement for the setting you want to work in — clinical, collegiate, commercial or corporate — because they hire from each other far less than students expect.

bodyHtml:
⚠⚠⚠ The job needs no degree. That is the whole shape of this page.

RoleSOCEntry educationMedianJobsOpenings/yrOutlook 2025–35
Exercise trainer / group fitness instructor39-9031⚠⚠ High school diploma$47,160388,400⚠ 68,000+7%
Exercise physiologist29-1128Bachelor’s$59,46021,2001,400⚠ +13%

⚠⚠⚠ 68,000 openings a year is one of the largest figures anywhere on this site — and the entry-level education is a high school diploma. No Florida licence exists for personal training. What the job actually requires is a certification: BLS says “personal trainers usually must be certified before they begin working with clients or with members of a gym or health club.”

So a Florida student in a kinesiology or exercise science degree needs to be able to answer a direct question: what is the degree for, given that the job at the end of it does not require one?

There are three good answers, and this page is organised around them:

  1. The clinical role. Exercise physiologist — bachelor’s entry, $59,460, and +13% growth, the fastest in this family. Chronic disease management, cardiac rehabilitation, clinical exercise testing.
  2. Graduate school. Physical therapy, occupational therapy, athletic training and physician assistant programmes draw heavily on this coursework. ⚠ The degree is a prerequisite package.
  3. Management. Running the facility rather than working the floor — and Florida awards more degrees in this than in exercise science.

⚠ If none of those three is the plan, get certified and start working. That is a legitimate answer, and four years of tuition is not a prerequisite for it.

⚠⚠ What Florida actually pays, and the part-time caveat that matters

Percentile (exercise trainers)FloridaUnited StatesDifference
10th$27,450$28,800−$1,350
⚠ 25th⚠ $28,970$35,280−$6,310
Median$38,800$47,160−$8,360
75th$52,630$61,730−$9,100
90th$72,870$83,100−$10,230

⚠⚠ Read the caveat before the numbers. This is an unusually part-time occupation — 55% work in fitness centres and 15% are self-employed — so annual figures mix full-time and part-time earners and understate the hourly rate. The national median works out at $22.67 an hour.

⚠⚠⚠ Even allowing for that, the Florida 25th percentile of $28,970 is below a full-time year at the state minimum wage — which tells you plainly that a quarter of this workforce is part-time, and that the bottom of this occupation is not a living on its own. The people earning the 75th and 90th percentile figures are almost all doing one of three things: specialising, building a client book as a sole trader, or managing.

⚠ The industry table is narrow and worth knowing anyway: government $48,300, fitness and recreational sports centres $48,140, educational services $45,350, civic and social organisations $38,640.

⚠⚠⚠ Two different degrees share this classification, and the bigger one is management

CodeDegreeFlorida outputWhere
31.0504⚠ Sport and Fitness Administration/Management833 at 8 institutionsUF 335, Florida State 268, UNF 57, UWF 24
31.0505Kinesiology and Exercise Science711 at 6 institutionsUCF 360, FAU 188, FGCU 70, UWF 64, USF 23, FIU 5
31.0501Health and Physical Education/Fitness, General58UWF 36, FAMU 22
⚠ 31.0507Physical Fitness Technician — the directly vocational one27 associate degreesNorthwest Florida 15, Chipola 5, Tallahassee 4, Pensacola State 3

⚠⚠ The largest degree in this family is a BUSINESS degree. Sport and fitness administration is marketing, finance, facility operations, event management and law — a perfectly good degree, and not a preparation for assessing a client or running a cardiac rehabilitation session. UF and Florida State together award 603 of them a year and award no exercise science bachelor’s under 31.0505 at all.

⚠⚠⚠ So “kinesiology” at UCF and “sport management” at UF are not versions of one thing. Decide which you want and then find the institution, rather than the other way round. Read the required-course list: if it has exercise physiology, biomechanics and anatomy, it is the science degree; if it has accounting, marketing and sport law, it is the management one.

⚠ And note the fourth row. Physical Fitness Technician is a two-year degree at four state colleges that exists specifically to produce working trainers — 27 graduates a year statewide. For someone whose plan is answer four above (get certified and work), it is a far cheaper route than a bachelor’s, and almost nobody is taking it.

⚠⚠⚠ The certification is the credential, so choose it deliberately

There is no Florida licence for personal trainers, and no programmatic accreditor for a fitness degree. What employers and insurers actually check is a certification, and they are not all equivalent. The distinction that matters is whether the certifying body is itself accredited — the recognised mark is NCCA accreditation, held by the major bodies (ACSM, NASM, ACE, NSCA and others).

⚠⚠ This is the same trap this site has now documented three times — in interior design, where the college is not the credential, and in chemistry, where the ACS approves the department but the student earns the certified degree. Here it is sharper: your degree is not the credential at all. A four-year kinesiology graduate and a certified trainer with no degree apply for the same floor job, and the certification is the part that is checked.

⚠ The degree’s advantage shows up one level up — clinical exercise physiology, strength and conditioning with a collegiate or professional team, cardiac rehabilitation, corporate wellness programme design, and graduate school. Those roles do read the transcript.

⚠ Exercise physiology is licensed in only one state (Louisiana), so in Florida the clinical roles are gated by employer requirements and certification rather than by law. Ask a prospective employer which certification they require BEFORE choosing which exam to sit; hospital-based cardiac rehabilitation and a commercial gym do not want the same one.

⚠⚠⚠ The most vocational courses in the prefix are the ones that do NOT transfer automatically

Almost every Florida course carries the statewide note “guaranteed transfer to institution offering same course.” PET is an exception, and the exceptions are not random: 13 of 122 active undergraduate PET numbers are marked NOT AUTOMATICALLY TRANSFERABLE — about 11%, against roughly 2% in a typical prefix.

And they cluster on exactly the courses this career is built from:

GroupNumbers
Exercise testing and fitness assessmentPET4550, PET4550L, PET4551, PET3551, PET2385
Athletic training clinical experiencePET3672, PET3673, PET3627C, PET4624, PET4625
Biomechanics and coachingPET3312C, PET4312, PET3765, PET4765

⚠⚠ The reason is not administrative sloppiness — it is that these are hands-on competency courses, and a receiving programme has to attest to your competence under its own standards. It cannot do that on another institution’s credit. The same logic appears in nursing, respiratory care and the other clinical fields on this site.

What to do about it: if you plan to transfer, take the assessment and clinical courses after you arrive at the institution you will graduate from, and take the transferable foundations — anatomy, physiology, nutrition, statistics, psychology — first. ⚠ Get a written answer before you enrol in a course that may not count.

⚠⚠ Two prefixes, and the anatomy trap that costs people a professional-school place

This family is taught under PET (physical education and coaching, more state colleges) and APK (applied kinesiology, almost entirely universities). Carrier counts are small throughout — PET2622 Care and Prevention of Athletic Injuries reaches nine institutions and nothing else in either prefix reaches five.

⚠⚠⚠ The trap is anatomy and physiology, and this site has documented it as the most damaging prefix divergence in Florida. The subject is taught as BSC2085C/BSC2086C and as APK2100C/APK2105C. Nearly every health-professions programme names the BSC numbers in its prerequisites, and a student who took the APK version may find it is not accepted.

⚠⚠ If physical therapy, occupational therapy, physician assistant or nursing is anywhere in your plan — and for a large share of kinesiology students it is — take the BSC sequence. The APK version is a good course and it is the wrong identifier to be holding at application time. Check the prerequisite list of a target programme literally, by number, in your first year.

What BLS says about AI here

⚠ Nothing on either page. Growth is attributed to gym membership, fitness classes, employer wellness programmes, obesity, and — specifically — “older adults who want low-impact forms of exercise and relief from arthritis and other ailments”, plus the rising prevalence of chronic conditions on the exercise physiology side.

⚠⚠ That is worth saying plainly: this is a career whose product is physical presence and personal accountability, and the federal projections show no technological dampening at all. The exposure here is to competition and to price, not to automation — which is a different problem and has a different answer: specialise, credential up, and move toward the clinical and management ends.

What to do first

  • ⚠⚠⚠ Answer the question the page opens with before you enrol: what is the degree FOR? Clinical, graduate school, management, or none of the three. If none, get certified and start working — the job does not require a degree.
  • ⚠⚠ Check whether your programme is kinesiology or sport MANAGEMENT. The larger of the two is management, and UF and Florida State award only that.
  • ⚠⚠ Take the BSC anatomy and physiology sequence, not the APK one, if any health profession is a possibility.
  • Get an NCCA-accredited certification while you are still a student, and ask target employers which one they want before you sit it.
  • ⚠ Sequence the assessment and clinical courses for the institution you will graduate from — they are the ones that do not transfer automatically.
  • Aim at exercise physiology if the science interests you: $59,460, +13%, and it reads the transcript.
  • Take statistics and a nutrition course. Assessment is measurement, and nutrition is the question every client asks first.
